title: In a Glass Darkly
creator: Joseph Sheridan Le Fanu
description: First collected edition in three volumes, containing “Green Tea,” “The Familiar,” “Mr. Justice Harbottle,” “The Room in the Dragon Volant,” and “Carmilla.” Published by Richard Bentley & Son.
subject: Irish Gothic fiction; ghost stories; supernatural fiction; Dr. Hesselius

title: Isle in the Water
creator: Katharine Tynan
description: A collection of fifteen short stories set primarily within Irish domestic, rural, coastal, and Catholic contexts, the collection explores grief, marriage, family conflict, religious belief, poverty, memory, social obligation, and the persistence of the dead within the lives of the living.
subject: Irish Gothic fiction; women’s writing; marriage; domestic haunting; spectrality
source: A. & C. Black (Adam and Charles Black)

title: Lord Arthur Savile’s Crime and Other Stories
creator: Oscar Wilde
description: First collected edition of Wilde’s stories, including “Lord Arthur Savile’s Crime,” “The Canterville Ghost,” “The Sphinx Without a Secret,” and “The Model Millionaire.” Published by James R. Osgood, McIlvaine & Co.
subject: Irish literature; Victorian short fiction; Gothic fiction; supernatural fiction; satire; crime

title: Holland-tide: Or, Munster Popular Tales
creator: Gerald Griffin
description: Collection of Irish regional tales associated with Munster. First published in London by W. Simpkin and R. Marshall; imprint identifies J. M’Creery as printer.
subject: Irish fiction; Munster folklore; regional literature; popular tales; national tale

title: Jason and Other Stories
creator: Bithia Mary Croker, usually credited as B. M. Croker
description: First collected edition of eight short stories, including supernatural and Anglo-Indian tales. Published in London by Chatto & Windus; the first edition is an octavo volume of 256 pages with a publisher’s catalogue dated March 1899.
subject: Anglo-Indian fiction; Irish women’s writing; colonial fiction; supernatural fiction; short stories; empire

title: The Brotherhood of the Seven Kings
creator: L. T. Meade and Robert Eustace
description: First book edition of the detective novel assembled from the preceding Strand Magazine serialization. Published in London by Ward, Lock & Co.
subject: Detective fiction; Victorian sensation fiction; crime fiction; secret societies; serial-to-book publication; popular literature
